title: CrossModal Study
description: This dataset comprises MEG recordings from a cross-modal target-discrimination study investigating alpha oscillations and frequency-tagged neural responses during auditory and visual target preparation. Participants were cued to attend to either auditory or visual targets, with a task-irrelevant 3-second interval featuring frequency-tagged visual (36 Hz) and auditory (40 Hz) stimulation prior to target onset. The study examined target discrimination performance under conditions with and without cross-modal distractors, recorded at the University of Birmingham, United Kingdom.
methods_description: Participants performed a cross-modal target-discrimination task in which cues indicated whether an upcoming target would be auditory (tone) or visual (Gabor patch/disc). During the cue-target interval (3 seconds), a fixation cross was frequency-tagged at 36 Hz while an amplitude-modulated 40 Hz tone was played. In Block 1, targets were presented without distractors; in Block 2, targets were accompanied by a distractor from the other sensory modality. Stimulus difficulty was individually calibrated for auditory and visual conditions prior to the main experiment. Eye-tracking (eye-link) data were also collected to monitor eye movements during MEG recording. One participant (sub-07) was excluded due to incomplete data collection and poor performance.
